Read the policy evidence

Square markers provide country-positioned references for international passenger rules. The evidence specifies the legal jurisdiction, including England-only measures. The groups affected and the exceptions changed over time. These selected national policies are separate from the land-border charts; they do not represent a comprehensive inventory of national travel rules or airport closures.

Open a policy to see its sources, dated changes and qualifications. An entry or departure restriction can apply while airports remain operational.

Australia closed its border to most foreign visitors during COVID-19NAT-AUS-ENTRY-COVID · 3 dated observations

Australia barred most non-resident foreign nationals from 20 March 2020 to reduce COVID-19 transmission. Citizens, permanent residents and other exempt travellers could still enter, subject to health rules. Entry reopened in stages: specified eligible visa holders from 15 December 2021, and all fully vaccinated visa holders from 21 February 2022. Unvaccinated visitors still needed an exemption. This was a border closure to the affected travellers, not a shutdown of every airport or a ban on all arrivals.

Displayed period
20 March 2020 – 21 February 2022
Meaning of these dates
Entry ban and staged reopening
Broad entry restrictions with changing exceptions. The final date marks reopening to all fully vaccinated visa holders, not removal of every border rule. No single closed-days total is assigned.

Australia restricted overseas departure by citizens and permanent residentsNAT-AUS-EXIT-COVID · 2 dated observations

From 25 March 2020, Australian citizens and permanent residents generally needed an exemption to leave the country by air or sea. Fully vaccinated eligible travellers no longer needed that departure exemption from 1 November 2021. Others still did. The map follows the broad restriction to this major relaxation, not to a claimed universal repeal; the final legal endpoint is not settled in this dataset.

Displayed period
25 March 2020 – 1 November 2021
Meaning of these dates
Departure ban to vaccinated-traveller relaxation
Exceptions and eligibility changed. The final date relaxed the rule for eligible vaccinated travellers; it was not the end for everyone. No exact duration or later status is inferred.

New Zealand closed its border to most foreign travellers during COVID-19NAT-NZL-ADMISSION-COVID · 4 dated observations

New Zealand restricted entry by most foreign travellers from 19 March 2020, while retaining return rights and specified exceptions. Admission later reopened through travel arrangements and different traveller groups. Australian citizens and permanent residents gained wider entry in April 2022, followed by eligible visa-waiver visitors in May. Remaining visitor and student visa categories reopened on 31 July 2022, alongside maritime reopening. This history does not mean that every traveller was excluded throughout, or that every airport stopped operating.

Displayed period
19 March 2020 – 31 July 2022
Meaning of these dates
Entry ban and phased reopening
Exceptions, travel arrangements and eligible groups changed. July 2022 reopened remaining visa categories and maritime arrivals; visa approval and health requirements still mattered. No continuous closed-days total is assigned.

UK COVID-19 arrival conditions: quarantine, testing and passenger formsNAT-GBR-ARRIVAL-CONDITIONS-COVID · 2 dated observations

UK-wide notices introduced isolation and passenger-information requirements in June 2020 and removed remaining COVID-19 testing and passenger-locator requirements in March 2022. These were conditions on admission, not a universal UK entry ban. Rules and enforcement differed between the UK nations and changed over time. This record shows the two documented changes, not an uninterrupted period with identical rules.

The map shows the documented observation dates only; this record does not establish a continuous interval.

England prohibited overseas departure without a permitted reasonR6-EU-004 · 2 dated observations

From 29 March 2021, England's regulations prohibited overseas departure without a permitted reason. The rule applied to air, sea and international rail departures; it was removed from 17 May 2021. This is the same policy already recorded for the Channel Tunnel, shown here with its wider England-only scope. It is not an extra independent closure and does not establish physical shutdown of airports or terminals.

Displayed period
29 March 2021 – 17 May 2021
Meaning of these dates
England overseas-departure prohibition
Dates mark commencement and removal of the legal provision, not measured interruption of every journey. England only; the other UK nations are not included. Linked to the existing land record R6-EU-004.

England restricted entry after travel through four red-list countriesNAT-GBR-ENG-REDLIST-COVID · 2 dated observations

From 9 April 2021, England refused entry to non-exempt visitors who had recently been in the Philippines, Pakistan, Kenya or Bangladesh. British and Irish citizens and people with UK residence rights were excepted, but faced hotel quarantine and testing. This was an entry prohibition for a defined traveller group, not a universal UK closure or a direct flight ban. The later amendment chain is incomplete, so this record appears only at its documented date.

The map shows the documented observation dates only; this record does not establish a continuous interval.
